title: Empirical integration of a formal network verifier as an oracle inside an LLM Generate–Verify–Repair loop for intent→configuration pipelines
research_question: Does embedding a formal-network verifier as an oracle inside a paired Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) loop increase detection/rejection of unsafe or incorrect LLM-generated network configurations and improve end-to-end repair success versus a generate-only baseline?
confirmatory_hypotheses: Embedding a formal verifier as an oracle in a GVR loop increases the proportion of unsafe or incorrect generated configurations that are detected and rejected relative to a generate-only baseline (paired estimand).

When the verifier rejects a candidate, a bounded automated LLM-guided repair loop (bounded attempts) will produce a verifier-accepted configuration within the preregistered repair budget more often than single-shot generation.
exploratory_questions: By how much do false-accept and false-reject rates (verifier vs. emulator ground truth) vary across vendor-style syntaxes and topology templates?
Does a conservative vs permissive verifier rule-set materially change measured repair success and false-accept rates?
benchmark_scope: SyntheticNetOpsIntentConfig_v1 (public synthetic intent→configuration suite produced and published with this study)
Emulator environment: Kathará/Mininet emulation images (Docker-based) for dynamic semantic ground-truth
model_scope: Single hosted LLM API (one model identifier; exact identifier logged in execution artifacts and Disclosure).
transformation_scope: Token-level canonical mapping between vendor syntaxes
primary_estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (paired difference in proportion of unsafe configs detected/rejected by the verifier in GVR arm minus baseline generate-only detection)
secondary_estimands: repair_success_probability_conditional_on_initial_reject (proportion of rejected tasks where bounded repair produced verifier-accepted config)
verifier_false_accept_rate (verifier accepted but emulator reports violation)
verifier_false_reject_rate (verifier rejected but emulator reports safe)
sampling_plan: Paired within-task design. N = 270 distinct intent→configuration tasks, constructed as 3 vendor-style syntaxes × 3 topology templates = 9 clusters × 30 tasks per cluster = 270 tasks. For each task both arms are executed (paired): (A) generate-only baseline: single generation attempt; (B) GVR: generate, verifier check, and if rejected invoke bounded repair loop (up to R attempts per task; R varies by budget scenario and is preregistered). Random seeds and deterministic prompt templates are fixed and recorded. Validation subset: 20% stratified sample (6 tasks per cluster × 9 clusters = 54 tasks) reserved for verifier-vs-emulator coverage validation (device-executed via emulator) and used to compute verifier false-accept/false-reject rates.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis executed by the registered executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' computing estimand 'paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline'. Primary treatment of failed model calls: 'complete_pair_primary' (see missingness_plan); sensitivity analysis with 'complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity' will be reported. Test: paired-proportion comparison (McNemar / paired binary analysis per registered contract) two-sided alpha=0.05 with 95% CIs. Report repair-success probability conditional on initial rejection and compute number-needed-to-repair. Subgroup analyses by vendor-style and topology (Bonferroni-corrected per multiplicity_plan). Report verifier false-accept and false-reject rates against emulator ground truth from the 54-task validation set and for the full dataset where emulator checks were performed. All analysis code and raw outputs are logged.
multiplicity_plan: Primary outcome is a single preregistered paired comparison. Nine preregistered subgroup comparisons (3 vendors × 3 topologies) will use Bonferroni correction: adjusted alpha = 0.05/9 = 0.0056. All secondary/exploratory analyses will be flagged as exploratory.
missingness_plan: Model/API call failures: deterministic retry policy of up to 2 retries per failed call with exponential backoff; retries are logged. If retries exhaust, treat the pair per the registered analysis primary option 'complete_pair_primary' (pair remains but primary estimand executor handles failure per contract). Sensitivity analysis will treat unresolved generation/repair failures as 'zero' successes ('complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity'). No manual human intervention is permitted; any task with infrastructure/emulator failure is recorded and excluded only if the failure prevents emulator ground-truth acquisition; exclusions and counts will be reported exactly.

risk_factors: Pre-lock development artifacts accidentally re-used in dataset (pre-lock rehearsals not to be used).
Duplicate or near-duplicate tasks leaking between validation/confirmatory sets.
RAG retrieval store contamination (e.g., containing test answers).
detection_procedures: Deterministic SHA-256 hashing of all prompts, intents, and retrieved documents recorded per invocation to detect reuse.
Automated exact and fuzzy duplicate detection (token-level Jaccard similarity threshold 0.9) across dataset and retrieval store.
Deterministic snapshotting of the RAG retrieval index at experiment start; index is frozen for all model calls.
item_flagging_rules: Exact-duplicate tasks flagged and excluded from confirmatory set automatically.
Near-duplicates exceeding similarity threshold are flagged and placed into a separate diagnostic set; flags are deterministic and recorded.
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Automatically exclude exact duplicates from primary analysis; report analyses with and without near-duplicate exclusions. Perform sensitivity analyses to quantify effects of duplicate exclusion.
residual_uncertainty: Undetected semantic near-duplicates below fuzzy threshold.
Potential retrieval-store content overlap with LLM training data (model nondeterminism and proprietary training data unknown).

budget_scenarios.description: Conservative worst-case: GVR repair budget R=3; retry policy as preregistered. Paired execution runs both arms for all N tasks.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-task worst-case model calls = baseline(1) + GVR(initial 1 + 3 repairs) = 5 calls; 270 tasks × 5 = 1350 calls. 1350 < capability manifest maximum_planned_model_calls (10000) and CPU/docker-based emulation fits within the 7-day wallclock with deterministic run scheduling.

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended pragmatic scenario (balanced cost/reliability): GVR repair budget R=2 (preregistered), retries and validation as specified.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-task worst-case model calls = baseline(1) + GVR(initial 1 + 2 repairs) = 4 calls; 270 × 4 = 1080 calls. This keeps headroom for API transient retries and logging while remaining well under the model-call cap and within 7-day execution budget. Recommended to balance evaluation power and cost.

budget_scenarios.description: Minimal / low-cost scenario: GVR limited to initial verify only (R=0), used as sensitivity/diagnostic arm when API cost or rate limits are binding.
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Per-task calls = baseline(1) + GVR(initial 1) = 2 calls; 270 × 2 = 540 calls. Useful as lower-cost sensitivity run; retains paired structure but does not evaluate repair efficacy.

power_plan.target_effect: Absolute difference of 0.10 (10 percentage points) in detection/rejection proportion between GVR and baseline
power_plan.calculation_method: Approximate paired binary-power calculation / McNemar-style sample-size reasoning using normal approximation under conservative assumptions (two-sided alpha=0.05, power=0.80). Exact test executed post-hoc via the registered analysis executor.
assumptions: Paired design with independent task pairs
Conservative baseline detector rate p0 ≈ 0.50 for sensitivity calculation (conservative for variance)
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With N=270 paired observations and conservative baseline p0≈0.50, the approximate minimum detectable absolute paired difference is ≈0.10 (10 percentage points) at 80% power under normal approximation assumptions. Exact confidence intervals and exact test p-values will be computed by the registered analysis executor.
sensitivity_analyses: Vary baseline p0 between 0.30 and 0.70 to quantify MDE changes.
Alternate failed-call treatment: treat unresolved calls as zero-success (sensitivity executor option).

semantic_equivalence_checks: For each transformation, run the transformed config in the emulator and compare emulator reachability/safety outputs with pre-transformation outputs on a diagnostic set; any semantic divergence is flagged automatically.
Automated diffing of control-plane relevant fields and deterministic acceptance thresholds applied; differences recorded
automatic_rejection_rules: If a transformation causes emulator-detected semantic changes for any task in the 100-item transformation test-suite, the transformation is rejected and removed from the pipeline automatically.
If syntax normalization introduces parse errors in target vendor syntax, the transformed output is rejected and original output is retained for diagnostics.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: 20% stratified audit: the 54-task validation subset (6 per cluster) is used for verifier-vs-emulator checks and transformation validation; all validation runs are recorded in full and hashes of artifacts are archived.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Mapping tables validated deterministically via a 100-sample synthetic suite covering common token patterns; all mapping changes are versioned and tested automatically in Dockerized unit tests.
residual_risks: Transformations that preserve high-level reachability but alter low-level vendor-specific operational side-effects undetected by emulator.
Edge-case vendor CLI constructs not exercised by synthetic mapping tests.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Emulator (Kathará/Mininet) approximations may not capture all production device stateful behaviors; conclusions are explicitly scoped to emulator-grounded behavior.
Verifier coverage: despite device-executed validation subset, the verifier may miss vendor-specific corner cases outside the validated sample.

Repair loop may overfit to the verifier rules and produce configs that pass verifier but fail in untested dynamic scenarios; mitigation: emulator checks and conservative verifier rule-set sensitivity analysis reduce but do not eliminate this risk.

Model API nondeterminism and proprietary training data: retrieval of model behavior variability may affect repeatability; logged seeds and full transcripts mitigate but cannot eliminate model nondeterminism.
Synthetic task suite may not fully represent production intent distribution; external generalization is therefore limited.
